items.title: Captain Verne Streckfus Interview, 1960-09-22
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Well, most of them, Louie Armstrong played by ear. When he came with us...

ctx.x: And, uh, we find that, uh, in our business today, why, that the people that come aboard the booth, uh, still like straight music the best. If you watch, uh, the people dance, the ones with the fathom and the rumblings and all the rest of them come along, they all walk off, and then the, uh, pretty music comes on, and even the waltz, why they'll, uh, come and kill the floor again. They still, the patrons that we have still like good dance for music. Pretty music. But good rhythm. Must have good rhythm. See? Well…

Well, most of them, Louie Armstrong played by ear. When he came with us, he couldn't read a note. And if he still doesn't, I don't know if he reads yet or not, but he didn't read music when, uh, came with us. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah.
Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah.
